overview: Nutrien Ltd., headquartered in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, is the world's largest provider of crop inputs and services, formed in 2018 from the merger of Agrium and PotashCorp. It operates an integrated model spanning upstream fertilizer manufacturing (the world's #1 potash producer and #2 North American nitrogen producer, plus a phosphate business under strategic review) and the world's #1 agricultural retail network (over 1,800 locations) selling crop nutrients, crop protection, seed and financing directly to farmers across North America, Australia and South America. Shares are dual-listed on the TSX and NYSE under NTR; the group reports in US dollars under IFRS.

business_model.summary: Nutrien earns money two ways: (1) upstream manufacturing and sale of potash, nitrogen and phosphate fertilizers, a commodity-cyclical, capital-intensive business where profitability is driven by global benchmark fertilizer prices versus natural gas/sulfur/mining-tax input costs and plant utilization; and (2) downstream Retail distribution of crop nutrients, crop protection, seed, merchandise and financing to farmers, a steadier, margin-stable business (~10% EBITDA margin) that management explicitly positions as a counter-cyclical stabilizer against upstream commodity swings. FY2025 segment adjusted EBITDA mix: Retail $1.74B (28%), Potash $2.25B (37%), Nitrogen $2.15B (35%), Phosphate $0.38B (6%), Corporate/Other/Eliminations -$0.47B. Revenue is largely transactional/seasonal (spring/fall application windows) rather than recurring, though Nutrien Financial's extended payment terms to growers create an interest-income-like recurring component (~$0.4B revenue). Customer base is overwhelmingly B2C/farmer-facing in Retail (>600,000 customer accounts) and B2B in the upstream segments (wholesale fertilizer buyers, Canpotex offshore distribution, industrial customers).

revenue_streams.name: Retail (crop nutrients, crop protection, seed, merchandise, services, Nutrien Financial)

business_model.customer_type: Retail: B2C/farmer direct (>600,000 accounts, >4,200 crop consultants) with embedded trade financing (Nutrien Financial). Upstream (Potash/Nitrogen/Phosphate): B2B wholesale, much of Potash exported via the Canpotex joint-venture marketing arm to 40+ countries (Latin America ~39%, other Asia ~29%, China ~11%, India ~6%).
business_model.geographic_mix: Upstream manufacturing concentrated in Canada (6 Saskatchewan potash mines) and the US (11 nitrogen facilities, 2 integrated phosphate complexes), plus a Trinidad nitrogen facility now shut down. Retail operates in North America, Australia and South America (Brazil is one of the largest and fastest-growing ag markets globally but carries greater credit/affordability risk).

main_competitors: regional/independent ag retailers (fragmented competitive set in Retail)
competitive_position.market_position: #1 global agricultural retailer, #1 global potash producer, #2 North American nitrogen producer. Potash supply is highly concentrated: Canada holds ~40% of global production capacity and Russia/Belarus together hold ~35%, making Nutrien one of a small number of low-cost, geopolitically stable suppliers.

moat_factors.factor: Resource scarcity / high barriers to new potash supply
moat_factors.description: High-quality potash reserves are concentrated in a handful of countries; a greenfield mine costs over $2,300/tonne of capacity and takes a minimum of 10 years to build, giving incumbents like Nutrien a structural head start even as BHP's Jansen project (Stage 1 ~84% complete as of mid-2026, targeting 4.15 Mtpa, Stage 2 bringing combined capacity to 8.5 Mtpa) prepares to enter the market.

moat_factors.factor: Low-cost North American natural gas feedstock
moat_factors.description: North American nitrogen operations (~85% of Nitrogen sales volumes) benefit from among the lowest-cost natural gas in the world versus European and Asian competitors, supporting a structural cost advantage.

moat_factors.factor: Scale and vertical integration across the ag value chain
moat_factors.description: Owning upstream manufacturing, midstream logistics (~5,600 owned/leased railcars, marine terminal access via Canpotex) and downstream retail gives Nutrien supply-chain optimization and the ability to capture margin at multiple points; Retail's counter-cyclical earnings profile smooths the upstream commodity cycle.

moat_factors.factor: Scale/reach in a fragmented Retail market
moat_factors.description: Agricultural retail is highly fragmented, dominated by small/medium competitors; Nutrien's scale, proprietary product portfolio (~1,700 proprietary crop nutrient, crop protection and seed products generating higher margins) and digital/agronomic services create switching costs for farmer customers, but the business is not a natural monopoly and must continually invest to retain share.

Over 4,200 crop consultants and embedded financing (Nutrien Financial) deepen the customer relationship, but farmer loyalty is price-sensitive and the input products themselves are largely commoditized.

weaknesses: Upstream segments are price-takers in global commodity markets with limited pricing power over benchmark potash/nitrogen/phosphate prices
Phosphate segment is sub-scale, lower-margin (6% of EBITDA) and under strategic review/possible sale, creating a smaller, less diversified upstream portfolio ahead
Trinidad nitrogen facility shut down in Q4 2025 due to gas supply/port access issues, a reminder of geopolitical/feedstock risk outside North America
Exposure to Brazil adds FX and farmer-credit/affordability risk (weaker affordability has driven a shift to lower-analysis, lower-margin nitrogen/phosphate products there)
New large-scale competitor (BHP Jansen) entering potash with a reportedly lower labor cost per tonne, a medium-term threat to Nutrien's relative cost position and pricing power

growth_drivers: Structural free cash flow growth strategy: 'simplify and focus, operational excellence, disciplined capital allocation' - ~$900M of gross divestiture proceeds since Q4 2024, ~$200M annualized cost savings surpassed

Retail EBITDA growth via proprietary product mix shift (proprietary products already ~24% of total Retail gross margin in 2025, up from 23%), Nutrien Financial expansion, and Brazil margin-improvement plan
Potash automation and debottlenecking (49% of ore tonnes mined using automation in 2025, more than double 2023) lowering controllable cash cost per tonne ($58/tonne in 2025)
Nitrogen reliability investments (92% ammonia operating rate in 2025, up from 88%) and low-cost debottlenecks at Redwater and Geismar increasing volumes without major new capex
Portfolio optimization: potential sale/restructuring of Phosphate business and Trinidad nitrogen operations to redeploy capital into higher-return core assets

Secular tailwind: rising global food demand, declining arable land per capita, and under-application of potash in emerging markets support multi-year fertilizer demand growth (global potash shipments guided to a fourth consecutive year of growth in 2026, 74-77 million tonnes)

Increasing cash returns to shareholders: ratable share buyback program (NCIB for up to 5% of shares approved Feb 2026) and consistent dividend growth (quarterly dividend raised to $0.55/share in 2026 from $0.545 in 2025)

business.description: Potash, nitrogen and phosphate net selling prices are set in global markets and swing significantly with supply/demand (e.g., FY2023 adjusted EBITDA of $4.9B after a post-2022 price collapse vs FY2022's $12.8B peak), directly driving Nutrien's earnings and cash flow.

BHP's Jansen project (Stage 1 ~84% complete mid-2026, ramping toward 4.15 Mtpa with Stage 2 to follow, total ~8.5 Mtpa, roughly 10% of current global supply) is expected to be a low-cost entrant into Saskatchewan potash, a medium-term threat to pricing and Nutrien's relative cost leadership.
Brazil retail exposure carries grower affordability and credit risk; weaker affordability has already driven a shift to lower-margin products and just-in-time purchasing.
Ongoing strategic review of Phosphate (~6% of EBITDA) and Trinidad nitrogen (shut down Oct 2025) creates execution and valuation uncertainty around potential divestitures.

financial.description: ~$12.0-14.7B total debt over FY2024-2025 and ~$0.65-0.75B guided 2026 finance costs; adjusted net debt/adjusted EBITDA was 1.8x at end-2025 (improving), but upstream cash flow volatility means leverage ratios can swing quickly in a down-cycle.

Multi-currency operations (CAD, AUD, BRL) create translation and transaction FX exposure even though USD is the functional/reporting currency; 2024 included a $220M loss on foreign currency derivatives in Brazil.

Nutrien Financial extends up to one-year payment terms to farmers; gross Nutrien Financial receivables were $3.16B at end-2025 with an allowance of $57M - historically low-default but sensitive to a farm-income downturn.

regulatory.description: US tariffs on Canadian potash imports and China's retaliatory tariffs on Canadian canola/peas, plus the broader US-China trade conflict (China paused US soybean purchases for ~5 months in 2025 before a 2028 purchase commitment, with a residual 10% supplemental tariff remaining) directly affect North American farmer economics and fertilizer demand/cost structure.
Higher provincial (Saskatchewan) mining taxes were cited as a drag on 2025 Potash segment results; policy changes to royalty/tax regimes are a recurring cost risk.
Changing environmental, climate and data-privacy regulation could raise compliance costs or restrict operations, per Nutrien's own enterprise risk disclosure.

macro.description: Management discloses a sensitivity of ±$180M adjusted EBITDA / ±$0.30 EPS per $1/MMBtu change in NYMEX natural gas; overall gas cost rose to $3.53/MMBtu in 2025 from $3.15 in 2024, driven by Henry Hub benchmarks.

macro.risk: Global crop price / farm income cycle
macro.description: Farmer purchasing of fertilizer and crop inputs is tied to crop prices and grower cash margins; depressed crop prices reduce both volumes and the farmer's willingness to pay for higher-analysis/proprietary products.

Belarus/Russia represent ~35% of global potash capacity and are subject to sanctions-related trade disruption; nitrogen and phosphate trade flows are also affected by Chinese export restrictions (DAP/MAP exports down ~40% in 2025) and broader geopolitical conflict.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global crop nutrient demand is expected to grow steadily, underpinned by rising food/feed/biofuel demand and declining arable land per capita. 2025 global demand: potash ~74.5 Mmt, nitrogen ~167 Mmt, phosphate ~52 Mmt. Potash shipments are guided to a fourth consecutive year of growth in 2026 (74-77 Mmt) with management describing 2026 fundamentals as 'relatively tight' as demand growth tests existing supply chain capacity - before BHP Jansen's new supply arrives at scale.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High in the upstream Potash/Nitrogen/Phosphate segments (benchmark commodity pricing, e.g., FY2022 EBITDA of $12.8B vs FY2023's $4.9B); materially lower in Retail, which management positions as a stabilizing, counter-cyclical earnings stream.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - Nutrien carries meaningful short- and long-term debt (weighted-average long-term debt rate ~5.0% in 2025) and Nutrien Financial's deemed cost of funding (average borrowing rate 5.0% in 2025, down from 5.6% in 2024) is directly tied to prevailing rates; farmer demand for financed purchases is also rate-sensitive.
key_input_costs: Sulfur (Phosphate input, cited as a 2025 margin headwind)

recent_developments.event: Completed controlled shutdown of the Trinidad Nitrogen facility due to unreliable/uneconomic natural gas supply and port access uncertainty; also ceased production at the New Madrid upgrade facility.

Initiated a strategic review of the Phosphate business (reconfiguration, partnership or potential sale); reported candidates include Mosaic, ICL Group, K+S and private equity, with the unit valued at roughly $2.4B by RBC and contributing only ~6% of EBITDA.

Sold remaining Sinofert investment and disposed of 50% equity ownership in Profertil, generating a gain on sale and ~$900M of gross divestiture proceeds since Q4 2024 as part of the 'simplify and focus' strategy.

Board approved a new normal course issuer bid for up to 5% of outstanding shares (commencing March 3, 2026) and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.55/share; issued 2026 guidance (Retail EBITDA $1.75-1.95B, Potash volumes 14.1-14.8 Mt, capex $2.0-2.1B).

Reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.61, missing consensus of $2.70; raised potash sales volume guidance to 14.2-14.8 Mt and lowered capex guidance to $1.95-2.05B, reflecting a capital-efficiency focus; increased share repurchase pace (~$82M in Q3-to-date as of early August).

US tariff policy and the broader US-China trade conflict continued to pressure North American farm economics; China resumed US soybean purchases in late 2025 after a ~5-month pause and committed to buy at least 25 Mmt/year through 2028, though a residual 10% supplemental tariff remains and Brazil has gained durable Chinese market share at the US's expense.

BHP's Jansen Stage 1 potash project reported ~84% complete as of June 30, 2026, with first production targeted for late 2026 and a multi-year ramp toward 4.15 Mtpa (Stage 2 to follow, combined 8.5 Mtpa) - a structural new-supply threat to the Canadian potash oligopoly Nutrien currently benefits from.

guidance.as_of: Q2 2026 (August 5, 2026) MD&A, updating FY2025 Annual Report guidance of February 18, 2026

items.notes: Midpoint assumes high-single-digit proprietary products gross margin growth, strong Australia demand, higher crop nutrient margins/tonne, and lower crop nutrient sales volumes vs. 2025.
Reflects strong offshore demand, consistent with global shipment outlook of 74-77 Mt.
Supported by planned reliability/debottlenecking; assumes no Trinidad/New Madrid production.
Focus on capital efficiency while structurally growing free cash flow.

items.metric: Effective tax rate on adjusted net earnings

guidance.management_commentary: Management (CEO Ken Seitz) reiterated the three-pronged strategy of simplify and focus, operational excellence, and disciplined capital allocation, targeting 'low-risk, structural free cash flow growth.' Q2 2026 commentary noted record first-half Potash sales volumes and a 6% YoY increase in H1 adjusted EBITDA, offset by softer Q2 standalone results as higher benchmark prices were outweighed by lower fertilizer volumes and higher sulfur costs. Management continues to prioritize ratable share buybacks aligned with free-cash-flow-per-share growth, reliable dividend growth, and completing the Phosphate strategic review and Trinidad options assessment during 2026.

bull_case: World's largest potash producer and ag retailer with structural cost advantages (low-cost North American gas for Nitrogen, top-tier Saskatchewan potash reserves) that are extremely difficult and slow (10+ years, $2,300+/tonne) for new entrants to replicate
Diversified, partially counter-cyclical earnings model: steady ~10%-margin Retail business smooths the volatility of the commodity-priced upstream segments and generates structural free cash flow

Multi-year secular tailwind from rising global food demand and under-applied potash/nitrogen in emerging markets, with 2026 marking a fourth consecutive year of potash shipment growth and management describing fundamentals as tight

Active portfolio optimization (divesting Phosphate/Trinidad, record $900M+ in divestiture proceeds since Q4 2024, ~$200M in annualized cost savings) should sharpen focus on the highest-return, lowest-cost assets and improve ROIC
Shareholder-friendly capital allocation: improving balance sheet (1.8x adjusted net debt/EBITDA), new 5%-of-shares buyback authorization, and a dividend raised every year since the 2018 merger
bear_case: BHP's Jansen project is a credible, well-capitalized new entrant (targeting ~8.5 Mtpa combined capacity, roughly 10% of current global supply, at a reportedly lower cost structure) that could pressure long-run potash prices and erode Nutrien's relative cost leadership over the next 3-5 years

Earnings remain highly cyclical and exposed to commodity benchmark prices and natural gas costs (disclosed sensitivity of ±$180M EBITDA per $1/MMBtu), as shown by the swing from $12.8B adjusted EBITDA in FY2022 to $4.9B in FY2023

Ongoing US-China and US-Canada tariff/trade frictions create a less predictable environment for North American farm income and fertilizer trade flows, with Brazil durably gaining Chinese soybean market share at the expense of US farmers Nutrien serves
Phosphate and Trinidad strategic reviews introduce near-term execution/valuation uncertainty, and a sale (if it happens) permanently shrinks segment diversification

Q2 2026 adjusted EPS missed consensus ($2.61 vs. $2.70 expected) on lower fertilizer volumes and higher sulfur costs, and analyst views on potash pricing are notably split (RBC/Oppenheimer bullish into $78-85 targets vs. UBS's Sell rating on concern the 2026 rally already priced in optimistic fundamentals ahead of later supply/price pressure)
